questions.question: In Module 1 (Legislative landscape), what is the primary significance of understanding 'how bills move' through the legislative process?

options.text: A. It enables advocates to bypass public committee hearings completely
B. It allows advocates to identify key intervention points, amendment windows, and procedural milestones where advocacy can effectively influence legislation
C. It guarantees that any bill drafted by social workers will be enacted without debate
D. It allows organizations to predict exact judicial court rulings on future legislation

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 1 covers how bills move so advocates understand procedural hurdles (first reading, committee review, floor debate) and identify the precise strategic moments to advocate.

questions.question: Why are legislative 'committees' considered critical gatekeepers in Module 1?

options.text: A. Committees exist solely to provide ceremonial press announcements for the legislative chamber
B. Committee chairs are appointed by lottery and hold no discretionary power over bill agendas
C. Committees examine bill details, hold public hearings, propose amendments, and have the power to advance, stall, or kill legislation before floor votes
D. Only judicial judges are permitted to testify before legislative committees

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 1 identifies committees as pivotal decision points where bills are scrutinized, amended, testified on, and where many bills either advance or fail.

questions.question: How does legislative 'timing' impact advocacy strategy according to Module 1?

options.text: A. Advocacy should only be launched after a bill has already been signed into law
B. Legislative calendars are completely unpredictable and have no bearing on campaign success
C. Bills can be introduced and voted upon on any day of the calendar year without restriction
D. Understanding session calendars, fiscal budget cycles, and filing deadlines ensures policy inputs are delivered when decision-makers are actively deliberating

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 1 stresses timing: coordinating advocacy with legislative calendars, filing deadlines, committee hearing schedules, and budget cycles to maximize impact.

questions.question: Why must advocates determine legislative 'jurisdiction' before launching a campaign (Module 1)?

options.text: A. To confirm whether the issue falls under municipal, provincial/state, or federal statutory authority, targeting the correct level of government
B. To determine whether the international court of justice can sponsor local municipal ordinances
C. To avoid communicating with elected representatives who reside in neighboring districts
D. Jurisdiction is irrelevant because any legislature can enact laws on any topic across any territory

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 1 emphasizes jurisdiction: targeting the appropriate level of government (local, state/provincial, national) with legal authority to enact the desired statutory or regulatory reform.

questions.question: In Module 2 (Advocacy strategy), what is the purpose of 'power mapping'?

options.text: A. Measuring the electrical grid capacity of government office buildings
B. Systematically identifying key decision-makers, their relationships, influencers, allies, opponents, and targets to formulate an effective influence strategy
C. Documenting personal financial assets of political candidates for campaign finance violations
D. Determining which advocacy organizations have the largest social media followings

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 2 defines power mapping as a strategic tool to analyze power dynamics, identifying who holds formal and informal influence over a specific legislative outcome.

questions.question: What is a primary benefit of forming a 'coalition' in legislative advocacy as described in Module 2?

options.text: A. Eliminating the need to establish shared principles or compromise between participating groups
B. Forcing all member organizations to merge their legal non-profit entities into a single corporation
C. Pooling diverse resources, broadening community representation, demonstrating widespread support, and amplifying collective advocacy power
D. Ensuring that only a single organization speaks or appears at legislative hearings

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 2 explores coalition practice: bringing together diverse organizations to leverage combined expertise, mobilize broader constituencies, and present unified power.

questions.question: What is the key element of crafting an effective advocacy 'message' under Module 2?

options.text: A. Using dense technical jargon that only academic researchers can decipher
B. Making unsubstantiated emotional attacks on political opponents
C. Focusing exclusively on organizational fundraising goals rather than community impact
D. Creating a concise, clear narrative combining compelling human stories, credible practice evidence, and an explicit, actionable 'ask'

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 2 emphasizes that compelling advocacy messages unite clear human impact, reliable practice evidence, and an unambiguous legislative request ('the ask').

questions.question: When meeting with an elected decision-maker (Module 2), how should advocates conduct the meeting?

options.text: A. Be punctual, state the specific legislative request early, share relevant local constituent evidence, listen respectfully, and agree on follow-up steps
B. Arrive unprepared and monopolize the meeting by debating unrelated partisan issues
C. Demand an immediate on-the-spot binding legal contract before leaving the office
D. Threaten public retribution if the decision-maker asks probing questions about bill costs

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 2 outlines meeting etiquette: professional preparation, concise presentation of the ask, grounding in constituent realities, active listening, and structured follow-up.

questions.question: In Module 3 (Campaign delivery), what does 'briefing decision makers' require of advocates?

options.text: A. Flooding legislative offices with thousands of duplicate automated spam faxes
B. Providing concise, objective, and timely policy briefs, one-pagers, and expert testimony highlighting how legislation affects real constituents
C. Withholding data regarding the fiscal cost of the proposed bill
D. Refusing to answer inquiries from legislative research staff

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 3 emphasizes that briefing decision-makers involves delivering high-quality, concise, credible evidence and policy one-pagers that directly inform legislative votes.

questions.question: How should advocates approach 'mobilising constituents' in Module 3?

options.text: A. Speaking over affected communities and dictating what they should demand from lawmakers
B. Paying actors to pose as concerned local community residents at public town halls
C. Empowering affected individuals and community members with information, tools, and platforms to speak in their own voices directly to elected leaders
D. Restricting constituent advocacy exclusively to signed pre-printed postcards

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 3 highlights ethical constituent mobilization: supporting community members and service users with skills and opportunities to share their authentic lived experiences.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'monitoring outcomes' during an advocacy campaign (Module 3)?

options.text: A. Ensuring that campaign staff receive permanent political appointments in government
B. Closing down the advocacy coalition as soon as the bill passes its first reading
C. Verifying that opposition groups have ceased all political activities
D. Tracking committee amendments, voting patterns, floor debates, and administrative rule-making to assess whether the policy intent was preserved

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 3 stresses monitoring: following bills through markups, floor votes, and regulatory implementation to ensure that legislative commitments are honored.

questions.question: When an active bill is unexpectedly stripped of its key funding provision during a committee markup, what does campaign 'adaptation' (Module 3) entail?

options.text: A. Convening coalition partners, reassessing leverage points, and pivoting campaign tactics to restore funding through floor amendments or future budget cycles
B. Continuing the exact same talking points as if no amendment had occurred
C. Immediately terminating all public advocacy on social work issues
D. Initiating personal legal lawsuits against individual committee members

questions.rationale: Rationale: Module 3 highlights adaptation: evaluating procedural setbacks dynamically, modifying messaging, and mobilizing alternative legislative remedies with coalition partners.

questions.question: A coalition partner suggests misrepresenting data regarding the cost of an opposition bill to gain an immediate media advantage. What is the correct response under Module 2 & 3 ethics?

options.text: A. Approve the tactic because winning the legislative campaign justifies any factual distortion
B. Reject the suggestion, uphold ethical advocacy principles, and insist on accurate, verified practice data to protect credibility and integrity
C. Remain silent while the partner organization broadcasts the false claims
D. Leak the fabricated figures anonymously to political blogs

questions.rationale: Rationale: Professional ethics in advocacy require strict adherence to truthfulness and credibility; fabricated claims destroy organizational integrity and violate social work standards.

questions.question: What legal requirement governing non-profit and charitable lobbying must social work practitioners respect under the Practice notice?

options.text: A. Charitable organizations are completely exempted from all lobbying laws and reporting rules
B. Non-profits are legally required to endorse specific political parties during general elections
C. Registered charities must comply with statutory limits on direct legislative lobbying and maintain strict non-partisan neutrality in electoral campaigns
D. Social workers are prohibited by law from meeting with any elected official

questions.rationale: Rationale: The Practice notice and professional guidelines mandate compliance with charity and lobbying laws governing one's jurisdiction, including non-partisan requirements.

questions.question: A practitioner experiences pressure from an organizational funder to withdraw legislative testimony supporting tenants' rights. How should the practitioner navigate this using the Learning sequence?

options.text: A. Falsify their written testimony to align with the funder's commercial interests
B. Publicly denigrate the funder on personal social media without supervisory awareness
C. Withdraw the testimony immediately without informing coalition partners or leadership
D. Pause, consult supervisory and institutional leadership, adhere to professional social work ethics and local procedures, and clarify organizational advocacy boundaries

questions.rationale: Rationale: When professional values clash with funding or external pressures, the practitioner must pause, consult supervision, examine legal/policy obligations, and maintain ethical boundaries.
